core.title: Keep product capability manifests and feature files cross-referenced both ways
core.given: The plan contains feature files and/or product capability manifests with feature-reference entries.
core.when: The planner authors, edits, moves, deletes or reviews any of them.
core.then: Every feature file is referenced by its product capability manifest's feature-reference collection, and every feature-reference entry resolves to an existing feature file.
prefer: Update the product capability manifest's feature references in the same change that adds, renames or removes a feature file.
Record an intentionally capability-less feature in the orphan-feature allow-list instead of leaving it silently unreferenced.
avoid: A feature file no product capability manifest lists (feature -> product capability gap).
A manifest feature reference pointing to a missing, renamed or deleted feature file (product capability -> feature gap).
Recording a feature that does belong to a product capability on the orphan-feature allow-list just to silence the coverage check.
unless: The feature is recorded in the orphan-feature allow-list (exempts only the feature -> product capability direction; manifest feature references must still resolve).
core.why: Coverage means each feature is referenced by its product capability and vice versa; a one-sided link leaves untracked features or dangling references, breaking plan traceability.
evidence: The feature -> product capability coverage check passes: every feature file is referenced by its product capability manifest (excluding orphan-allow-listed features).
The product capability -> feature coverage check passes: every capability-manifest feature reference has a corresponding feature file.
verification: Two repository-wide coverage checks over the plan tree: direction feature -> product capability — every feature file must be referenced by its product capability manifest, with the orphan-feature allow-list as the only exception; direction product capability -> feature — every manifest feature reference must resolve to an existing feature file, with no exceptions authored. The manifest field that holds the feature references is stack data supplied by the profile, not rule text.
The allow-list exemption is one-directional: it never excuses a dangling manifest feature reference, and the product capability -> feature direction admits no exceptions.
Per-rule disposition: documentation-only — the obligation guides authors and reviewers; the checks report coverage gaps rather than block.
Out of scope: references between a product capability and its parent (user/system flow) artifacts, which belong to the parent-level coverage convention.

fires: The planner adds a new feature file without adding it to its product capability manifest's feature references.
The planner adds a manifest feature reference pointing to a feature file that does not exist.
The planner renames or deletes a feature file, leaving a stale manifest feature reference.
The planner edits or reviews a plan where a pre-existing feature file is not referenced by its product capability manifest, even with no structural edit and no coverage check run yet.

The planner inspects a product capability manifest (including one whose product capability has no feature files) containing a dangling feature reference, with no current structural edit or coverage finding.
A feature file exists (not allow-listed) whose product capability manifest is missing or does not list it.
A coverage check reports an unreferenced feature or a dangling capability-manifest feature reference.
doesNotFire: The feature file is recorded in the orphan-feature allow-list (exempts the feature -> product capability direction only).
Edits to user/system flow <-> product capability references only (covered by the parent-level, user/system flow coverage convention).
Content-only edits to a feature file when every feature file is already listed by its product capability and every manifest feature reference already resolves.

profileRequirements.meaning: The capability-manifest containment field that enumerates the product capability's features — the manifest's feature-reference collection whose entries the rule compares in both directions. The core speaks only of 'manifest feature references'; the concrete field name is stack data, so a stack with a differently named manifest reference field instantiates the same core.
profileRequirements.bunValue: features[] (the product capability manifest's features list; bun.json: 'product capability manifests with features[] entries')

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds this rule links — the product capability manifest (with its feature-reference collection) and the feature file. The core activates on the neutral kinds capability_manifest and feature_file; the profile maps them to the stack's concrete artifact kinds (in Bun, feature_file -> feature_yaml). Presence of either kind activates the rule and is what the coverage checks compare.
How feature files and product capability manifests are recognized as plan artifacts on disk (suffix or name pattern); the concrete serialization (YAML) is known only here, never in the core.
The plan tree the bidirectional coverage checks scan for product capability manifests and feature files.
profileRequirements.bunValue: plan tree (bun.json: 'The plan contains feature YAML files and/or product capability manifests...', 'a feature YAML file in the plan tree')

profileRequirements.meaning: The named allow-list in which intentionally capability-less features are recorded, exempting them from the feature -> product capability direction only.

neutralityNotes: Product capability, feature, user/system flow and 'the plan' are plan-structure vocabulary shared across stacks (cf. the layout and urn profile groups), so they remain in the core. Every other concrete fact is profile data: the manifest's feature-reference collection is supplied by roles.plan_hierarchy#feature_references (Bun: the features[] field), so a stack with a differently named manifest reference field instantiates the same core; the artifact kinds and their YAML serialization by roles.plan_artifact.kinds (feature_file -> feature_yaml) and suffix.plan_artifact; the plan tree by roots.plan; the orphan allow-list name by enforcement.exceptions#allowlists (Bun: features_orphaned). No literal schema field name, suffix, stack, runtime or path appears in the core. Validator and finding ids (test_all_features_in_capability_manifest, test_all_capability_feature_refs_exist) and the term id capability_feature_coverage are realization details and remain bunOnly. bun.json's per-fact activation notes are preserved elsewhere rather than as note fields on the core facts: 'either kind alone suffices' by core.given, 'the invariant holds continuously, not only on structural edits' by fires[3] and fires[4], and 'change/finding facts are additional triggers, not required for firing' by their needs_new_observer observability plus fires[6]. How a feature's owning product capability is determined and how a manifest feature reference resolves to a file (path or identifier) are not specified by bun.json, so the core leaves them to the realization's checks.
